newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures close down, December new benchmark.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures close down, December new benchmark.

text.p: The Japanese government bond futures market edged down in quiet trading on Monday, with the long-awaited shift in benchmark status from the current key September contract to the December the main news.
Trade volume of the December contract exceeded that of the September contract for the first time at the close, an event which is regarded as defining a benchmark shift.

Otherwise the market was sullen, marking time before the release of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) 'tankan' corporate sentiment survey. The September contract ended 0.15 down at 120.75, in volume of 18,723 contracts.
The December contract, meanwhile, edged down 0.06 to 119.50. Its volume was 28,410 contracts.

Both contracts slipped early in the morning, taking their cue from a fall in U.S. Treasuries last Friday. Thereafter the market saw little movement, hovering feebly in the negative region for most of trading time.
"There won't be much buying before the 'tankan' survey," said a dealer at a city bank's securities affiliate.
Dealers said there was sporadic talk in the market that the survey, due out on Wednesday, could be worse than earlier expectations.
Private think-tanks' forecasts for the tankan's diffusion index of major manufacturers, a key measure of the health of the economy, centres around zero, ranging from minus two to plus five.
The market is unlikely to become lively until the survey is released, as investors would rather make moves after they see the results, dealers said.

While few participants were reluctant to bid up the contract, there were very few incentives to sell in the market, dealers also said. "There is anticipation among dealers that some investors have to buy bonds," said a dealer.
In the cash bond market, the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGBs were yielding 3.110 percent, up 0.040 from Friday.
The 173rd 10-year JGBs were noticeably weak, said a dealer at a trust bank's securities unit. He said this might be due to selling linked to options.
